name: a_sector_hardware_networking
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Company news: IT hardware, networking, data-center and power-equipment.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Every material company-specific news item for US-listed IT hardware, networking, data-center and power-equipment companies >= $1B in the window, as many as you can find: press releases, 8-K filings, executive changes, activist campaigns, legal settlements, contracts, product launches, guidance, analyst rating/PT changes (firm, old → new), and the stock move. One bullet per company.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **APLD** — AI Infrastructure
- Applied Digital announced on October 2 that the second phase of Building 2 at its Polaris Forge 1 campus reached “Ready for Service,” adding **75 MW** of critical IT load across three 25-MW data halls; Building 2 reached **150 MW**, and fully operational critical IT load at the campus reached **250 MW** (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 2; reported Oct. 4).  
- Applied Digital’s Nasdaq-listed shares were reported in connection with the announcement, but the available source did not provide a verified October 5 price or percentage move as of 12:20 ET (source information available by Oct. 4).

## **HPE** — AI Infrastructure / Communications & Networking
- Hewlett Packard Enterprise received a reported **$1.2 billion** order from Vultr for AMD Helios AI servers; the deployment was described as the first commercial use of HPE’s Helios racks, combining AMD processors, HPE compute, liquid cooling and HPE Networking hardware (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2, 18:09 ET; report updated Oct. 4).  
- At an October 5 Networking Investor Day, HPE said cumulative fiscal-2026 AI-networking orders were expected to exceed **$3 billion**, projected fiscal-2027 networking-revenue growth in the **high-teens to low-20% range**, and projected data-center-networking revenue to grow at approximately **50% CAGR through fiscal 2029** (source report, Oct. 5, before 12:20 ET).  
- HPE reportedly raised its expected Juniper Networks integration synergies to **$800 million**; the available source did not specify the prior estimate or provide a verified October 5 stock move by 12:20 ET (source report, Oct. 5, before 12:20 ET).

## **AVGO** — Semiconductors / AI Infrastructure
- A filing disclosed that Broadcom agreed to provide Anthropic with up to **$42 billion** in convertible-note financing for infrastructure spending tied to Anthropic’s five-year commitment to lease **$125.2 billion** of TPU computing capacity; the disclosure also identified Broadcom’s combined roles as hardware supplier, equipment lessor and financier (Reuters report, Oct. 5, before 12:20 ET; agreement dated Oct. 1).  
- The report said the potential financing would cover approximately **one-third** of Anthropic’s TPU-lease commitment; the available source did not provide a verified October 5 stock move by 12:20 ET (Reuters report, Oct. 5, before 12:20 ET).

## **MTSI** — Optical & Photonics
- MACOM Technology Solutions was reported to have launched a **3.2-terabit optical chipset** for AI-data-center interconnects; the available report also said BMO Capital upgraded MACOM to **Outperform**, but did not state the prior rating or a price target change (TradingKey, Oct. 2; source updated Oct. 5).  
- MACOM shares rose **7.48%** on October 2, according to the available market report (TradingKey, Oct. 2).

## LS Electric — Power & Wide-Bandgap
- LS Electric announced a **$133.41 million** contract, equivalent to **180 billion won**, to supply **345-kV ultra-high-voltage transformers** for a North American hyperscale AI-data-center project; the announcement was dated October 1 and reported during the requested window (Yonhap, Oct. 5, before 12:20 ET).  
- LS Electric is not identified in the available results as a US-listed company, so its eligibility under the US-listing requirement could not be independently verified from the gathered material (Yonhap, Oct. 5).

## **EFXT** — AI Infrastructure / Power Equipment
- Enerflex announced an approximately **450-MW** natural-gas-fired power-generation equipment project for a North American data-center developer, with deliveries scheduled for **2027–2028** and approximately **$15 million** of 2026 capital spending; the announcement was dated October 1, outside the stated publication window, and was only surfaced in window-period coverage (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 1; source report available Oct. 5).  
- The available result identified Enerflex’s US ticker as **EFXT**, but did not provide a verified October 2–5 share-price move (source report, Oct. 5).

## Data-center sector — Macro / Calendar
- Goldman Sachs raised its **2026 year-end US data-center-capacity forecast by 5 GW to 64 GW**, cut its 2027 forecast by **5 GW to 90 GW**, and forecast US data-center power demand growth of **38%**, equal to **12 GW in 2026** and **17 GW in 2027** (Reuters, Oct. 5, 09:06 ET).  
- Reuters reported that a June Reuters/Ipsos poll found **14%** of respondents supported a data center being built in their community for technology-company AI projects (Reuters, Oct. 5, 09:06 ET).
